title: Enforce descriptive hypothesis/confound/run labels over opaque short codes
body: Claim-tier IDs like H1, C1, m3, m2.7 are fine as internal references but add cognitive load when humans read claim reports, lint output, or conclude-gate feedback. Investigate enforcing or encouraging descriptive labels (e.g. 'H_information_symmetry', 'C_topology_coupling') alongside short codes, or requiring a `label` field in [[hypotheses]] and [[confounds]] blocks that is used in human-facing output (lint warnings, claim-coverage report, conclude verdict) while the short ID is used for machine cross-referencing. Could be a Tier-1 lint rule (warn if id matches /^[A-Z][0-9]+$/ with no label field), a scaffold default, or a claim validate check.

title: Compose fast-and-frugal trees (FFTs) to guide experiment design decisions; land AFTER the metascience corpus
body: [task_id 261105_fft-design-decisions] Compose FFTs (fast-and-frugal trees: ordered binary cues, an exit at every node) as decision aids for design choices that are uncertain at pre-registration time. Example: when we are unsure what threshold to set in [outcomes], or which ladder of values of a design parameter to run, the tree should route to an exploratory assessment (a small, explicitly exploratory stage) instead of guessing a value into a confirmatory sidecar. Candidate cues: is the cutoff's basis cited, is there a pilot or prior-run distribution, is the parameter's effect range known, what does a wrong rung cost. Builds on existing FFT work (praxia:developing-fast-frugal-trees) and bathos conventions on exploration stages and threshold-cutoff skepticism, so exploratory runs stay exploratory and never leak into confirmatory claims. SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT: land AFTER the metascience corpus whose ingestion is currently in progress has landed. The corpus should inform which cues and thresholds the trees use, so derive them from the literature rather than guess. Do not start design or implementation before then.

title: bth cold: accept xtrax-packed units as archive members
body: Owner item (from asr task 261116_topology-scoping; scoping note asr .praxia/docs/research/261123_tier1-step-zero-archive-scoping.md). bth cold (output_tiers/archive.py build_archive) re-hashes loose reference files into run-<id>.tar.zst. Campaign outputs packed by xtrax.pack (members.tar.zst + members.idx.json + unit.json, format alynxr.unit_pack/1, content_digest over uncompressed members) would have to be unpacked first. Proposal: let a reference entry be an xtrax unit verified by its unit.json content_digest/record_digest (xtrax.pack.record_problem) instead of loose-file sha256, so packed units go cold as-is. Shipped in commit 5a440137 (v0.18.0) via interim swappable UnitPackReader / InterimUnitPackReader in src/bathos/output_tiers/unit_pack_reader.py (integrated into src/bathos/output_tiers/archive.py build_archive), ready to be repointed to cisternal.
